Equipment items and units

Splitting what it is (a new item, such as “QSC K12.2”) from what we own (an existing asset row, now a unit or a lot), so serial numbers, tags, quantities and kits work properly. Each screen below uses Cameron’s examples: the K12.2 PA kit, the XLR Cable Box, the Small XLR Cable Box packed at checkout, the PA Rack, and the six Chauvet Intimidator Trios bought on one line.

Item
Item: what it is. Model, category, type. Quantity is counted from its units and lots.
Unit
Unit: one physical thing with a serial number or tag. Quantity is always 1.
Lot
Lot: several identical untagged things, counted together, such as 10 untagged cables.
Any
“N × any”: a kit entry for how many of an item; scans decide which.
Screen 1
Equipment list

Items with their units and lots, worked-out counts, availability, and a flat view for finding a serial or tag.
Screen 2
Item page

Shared fields once; the units and lots table; which kits use the item and how.
Screen 3
Unit / lot form

Unit or lot first; serial or tag locks quantity to 1; purchase link; recovery period when depreciated.
Screen 4
Purchase review

One line of 6 Trios creates 6 units: pick or create the item, enter serials or tags, or keep a lot.
Screen 5
Kit editor

“N × any” or a specific unit or lot; Items kits confirm each line, containers scan as one.
Screen 6
Packing list and gig equipment

“2 × QSC K12.2” filled in by scans, container progress, and the printout with write-in blanks.
Screen 7
Scanning / pull

Tagged items are scanned (the K12.2s); untagged ones are counted, with a counter that starts full.
Screen 8
Locations and tracking override

Counts per place (#160) and overrides that move part of a lot.
Screen 9
Maintenance

Units in maintenance by tag and serial: edit notes, location and expected-back date, or return to service. Sent there while scanning.
Screen 10
Dashboard totals and overlap warning

Dashboard total = the sum of unit and lot replacement values (#157); conflicts counted per item.
Screen 11
CSV import

Template grouped by item / unit or lot / purchase; “;”-separated serials; serial-with-quantity guard.
